relevance_note: Case report of two Japanese FLD patients with LCAT variants and their tested relatives: 'Case 1 had a C to T nucleotide substitution in Exon 2 resulting in Pro69Leu [c.278 C>T (p.Pro69Leu)]'.
method_note: Hand-read the paper; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from values I transcribed, and every span was checked verbatim against the Markdown. Table 1 has patients as columns (headers: Normal values | Case 1 | Case 2 | Mother of Case 2); spans quote the row label through the person's cell. Lab-based checklist statuses (low apo A-I/A-II, hypertriglyceridemia excluded, and the Mother of Case 2's normal HDL, apo A-I/A-II, LDL/apo B, TG) were read against the table's printed 'Normal values' column; the authors comment in text only on LDL-C, HDL-C, FC/TC and RemL-C. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) Case 2 zygosity: text 'Both cases showed homozygous mutation' and the Fig. 1 legend ('homozygous mutation of proband') vs Table 1 row c.950 T>C giving 'Heterozygous' for Case 2; zygosity left 'not reported' for Case 2. (2) Case 1 parents: 'their parents showed heterozygous mutation' vs 'genomic DNAs were not available from the deceased father'; the father is given a row (deceased) but no variant row; mother of Case 1 recorded heterozygous from the parents statement and Fig. 1 legend. (3) Both parents of Case 2 are stated heterozygous, so inheritance 'inherited maternal' for the homozygous probands is a partial description (the enum has no biallelic option); for Case 1 only the mother is supported. Labels: 'parent of Case 2' is the second parent of Case 2 (the other is the Table 1 column 'Mother of Case 2'); the paper does not state this parent's sex in text. Not extracted: an 'elder sister' heterozygous carrier named only in the Fig. 1 legend ('Heterozygous mutation of mother and elder sister ... shown in Cases 1 (C) and 2 (D)'), because the legend does not say which proband she belongs to. APOE genotypes (modifier gene, common polymorphism) were not recorded as variant rows. Case 1 'no other abnormal findings' on physical examination excludes nothing specific. Normal renal function was recorded as 'impaired renal function' excluded, but the checklist item 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure' was left not reported because proteinuria was present and normal function does not address CKD. 'elevated unesterified (free) cholesterol' left not reported: absolute FC is near or within the printed range (61 and 50 vs 25–60) while the FC/TC ratio is high; the high ratio was mapped to 'reduced cholesteryl ester fraction'. Hemolytic anemia for Case 1 comes from statements about both patients (abstract); his case text says normochromic-normocytic anemia. Half-normal LCAT activity 'suggesting the diagnosis of FED' while authors label both FLD; disease label recorded as FLD.
